learning_outcomes.text: Know how matter is organized. Starting from atoms and their structure, have notions on the assembly of atoms in molecules and in crystallized solids.
Be able to apply stoichiometry rules and oxidation number variations to balance chemical reactions involving different states of matter (solid, liquid, gas).
Acquire work methods and autonomy in direct connection with the University Methodology UE.
Consolidate experimental know-how acquired in high school: common manipulations using usual chemical glassware and exploitation of measurement series.
Know and apply safety rules in a practical work room, be able to identify safety pictograms.

syllabus_topics: Crystallography (fcc, bcc, hcp): Structure of crystallized solids
Atomistics (the atom, hydrogen atom spectrum, electronic configuration of elements, understanding of periodic classification, electronegativity)
assessment_rules: For the main session, there are two continuous assessment written exams (weighted 0.25 and 0.5) and five continuous assessment deliverables (weighted 0.25). For the resit session, continuous assessment becomes integral. The lesser written exam receives a coefficient of 0.2, and the better written exam receives a coefficient of 0.3.
degree: Licence Sciences pour l'ingénieur — Génie mécanique (parcours Mécanique), UFR ST
